season.evidence: Only 10 logged ascents: Jul 1, Aug 7, Sep 2. Searches (Mountaineers Bailey Range pages, WTA/other Bailey traverse reports, guide trip listings) put the traverse in July to early August once the snowfields are passable. Stored Jul-Sep, mid-Jul to mid-Aug prime, confirmed.

otherTracksConsidered.why: 11 Aug 2025 summited, but it is a camp-based day (starts at a high camp 47.8371,-123.5697, ends 5 km south), not a trailhead round trip or trailhead-to-summit, and the report says the climber took a west-side line to the summit and came back down the east ridge. Not our stored east-ridge line end to end.
Aug 2023, turned back at the false summit.
4 Jul 2026 summited per the report, but no track in the packet; used only for facts.

facts.text: On the traverse to the true summit, one downclimb of a 5-6 ft wall just before the deepest notch is the hardest move (about mid class 4); most else is class 3+ ledges loaded with loose rock.
Near the top the north side of the ridge held slightly better rock than the south side.
In August a western line up the broken ridge cliffed out in a gully and cost far more time than the east approach to the summit; stay on the east.

notes: Single route on the peak, so identity is not the question; the harvested tracks just are not trailhead round trips. The Trailhead pin (47.9548,-123.8349) is some 24 km from the recordings' start; the route is a multi-day Bailey traverse so this is expected, not verified. No pin change proposed.
